name: IT-Vault
description: IT-Vault is a self-hosted IT asset register and helpdesk for whoever IS the IT department: assets, employees, contracts, tickets, a public request portal, LDAP/AD sync, network scanning, printable QR labels and e-signed handovers. IT-VAULT BRINGS NO DATABASE OF ITS OWN. Install MariaDB first (the MariaDB template in Community Applications is fine), then create an empty database and a user for it: CREATE DATABASE itvault CHARACTER SET utf8mb4; CREATE USER 'itvault'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY 'a-strong-password'; GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON itvault.* TO 'itvault'@'%'; Then either fill in the DB fields below, or leave them empty and the first-run wizard will ask. The schema builds itself on first start and migrates itself on every update -- there is nothing to run by hand. The three paths below keep your data outside the image, so updating replaces the container without touching anything: /app/data holds the session key and the database pointer, /app/invoices the attachments, /app/backups the scheduled backups. First run: open the WebUI and the setup wizard creates your admin account. There is no default password.

paths.name: Data
paths.description: Session key and the saved database pointer. Keep this: losing it signs everyone out and forgets which database to use.

paths.name: Invoices
paths.description: Invoices and proof-of-purchase files attached to assets.

paths.name: Backups
paths.description: Where scheduled backups are written. Put this on a share you actually back up.

ports.name: WebUI Port
ports.description: The port you will open IT-Vault on.

variables.name: Database host
variables.description: Your MariaDB/MySQL server. For a MariaDB container on this Unraid box, use the server's LAN IP (bridge networking cannot reach it by container name). Leave empty to be asked by the setup wizard instead.

variables.name: Database name
variables.description: The empty database you created for IT-Vault.

variables.name: Database user
variables.description: A user with rights on that database -- not root.

variables.name: Public URL
variables.description: The address people reach this on from outside, e.g. https://itvault.example.com. Used for the links in acknowledgement and portal emails, which are useless if they point at a LAN address. Leave empty if you only use it on the LAN.

variables.name: Force secure cookies
variables.description: Set to 1 to insist the session cookie is only ever sent over HTTPS. Leave empty and it is decided per request, which is right if you reach it both ways.

variables.name: Session secret
variables.description: Leave empty. IT-Vault generates a strong one on first start and keeps it in the data path above, which beats any value typed into a template -- a known secret lets anyone forge an admin session. Set it only to share one key across several instances.
